sections.readable_text: Some key characteristics about [MATH: y=\sec x] are:

sections.normalized_html:
• The domain of the function is almost [MATH: x\in (-\infty ,\infty)] except for the points where the function is undefined, namely [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots]

  • The range of the function is [MATH: y\in (-\infty,-1] \cup [1, +\infty).]

  • The period of the function is [MATH: 2\pi.]

  • It has no zeros and no global extrema.

  • The branches of the function alternate between positive and negative, with a positive branch in [MATH: \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right).]

  • The graph has vertical asymptotes at the points not in the domain: [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots.]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's recall the graph of [MATH: y=\sec x.]

Note that the range of the function is [MATH: (-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty),] so [MATH: y=\sec x] takes any value [MATH: y\leq -1] and any value [MATH: y\geq 1.]

Therefore, the values [MATH: y=1] and [MATH: y=2] belong to the range, [MATH: y=0] is not in the range.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The secant is the reciprocal of the cosine:
[MATH: \sec x = \dfrac{1}{\cos x}.]

Content:
To plot the graph of [MATH: y=\sec x,] with [MATH: x] in radians, we create a table with some known values:

Content:
| [MATH: x] | [MATH: -\frac\pi 3] | [MATH: -\frac\pi 4] | [MATH: -\frac\pi 6] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: \frac\pi 6] | [MATH: \frac\pi 4] | [MATH: \frac\pi 3] | [MATH: \frac\pi 2] | [MATH: \frac{3\pi} 4] | [MATH: \pi] | [MATH: \frac{5\pi} 4] | [MATH: \frac{3\pi} 2] |
| [MATH: \cos x] | [MATH: \frac{1}{2}] | [MATH: \frac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}] | [MATH: \frac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: \frac{1}{2}] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -\frac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\frac{\sqrt 2}{2}] | [MATH: 0] |
| [MATH: \sec x] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: \sqrt 2] | [MATH: \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}] | [MATH: \sqrt 2] | [MATH: 2] | undef. | [MATH: -\sqrt 2] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -\sqrt 2] | undef. |

Plotting these points, we get the following curve:

[IMG: /graphics/016d3649daaca30fd645fe56d8a0cfa5]

Content:
Since the period of [MATH: \cos x] is [MATH: 2\pi,] the period of [MATH: \sec x] is also [MATH: 2\pi.] Since [MATH: \cos x] is an even function, the function [MATH: \sec x] is even. So we extend the plot with this periodicity property.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/9315f623ee4d41f160f938aad790b4ec]

Content:
- The domain of the function is almost [MATH: x\in (-\infty ,\infty)] except for the points where the function is undefined, namely [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots]

- The graph has vertical asymptotes at the points not in the domain: [MATH: x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{2},\pm\dfrac{3\pi}{2},\dots.]
